Status: the specific JSONHTL documentation and compatibility improvements are complete. The assessment and recommendations above are retained as the historical motivation.

items: Registry created at README/jsonhtl-extensions and linked from README, README/format, JSONHTL_SPEC and JSONHTL_SCHEMA.
JSONHTL_SPEC advanced to 0.5; registered extension grammar, shorthand, aliases, malformed/unknown handling, section-level defaults and consumer fallbacks documented.
Schema reconciled with table captions, string/integer version metadata, typed list items and registered strong/em/italic inline forms.
lint_jsonhtl.py added: live/offline schema, --key/--file/--all, recursive aliases, runnable cross-field checks and name uniqueness, table width, optional metadata and internal-link checks.
Web and desktop renderer changes reconciled against the live branch, preserving its existing sections, inline-cell support and aliases. Captions and section depth through details corrected.
Older local desktop variants and shared Envoy HTML renderer updated; static exporter inherits shared support for sections, details, SVG/images, inline emphasis and linked cells.

73 release tests passed; spec/schema/registry lint clean; live renderer and public note pages verified. Gdata release a5b3738 deployed to gravlax and service restarted. Shared renderer changes committed locally in Envoy as f3c5c91; pre-existing working-tree changes preserved.

para: Separate remaining work: full corpus cleanup, automatic alias normalisation, linter enforcement in write paths, and native desktop collapse controls. Internal-link checks identify unresolved targets; detecting actual orphaned notes requires a separate incoming-link graph audit. Shared-renderer/exporter changes are active locally; running desktop viewers need reopening to load changed Python code.

Assessment from 2026-05-28: JSONHTL is broadly well documented for its current size and purpose. The core model is clear, minimal, and LLM-friendly. The main documentation risk is undocumented extensions that have grown around the base format.
